# 2026 General Election Voter Guide: Representative in Congress, Florida District 3

The November 3, 2026, general election for Florida's 3rd Congressional District features a three-way contest to represent a diverse geographic constituency spanning North Central Florida. The district boundaries encompass Alachua, Baker, Bradford, Columbia, Dixie, Gilchrist, Hamilton, Lafayette, Levy, Marion, Suwannee, and Union counties [1, 2]. Historically, the district has leaned conservative, carrying a Cook Partisan Voter Index (CPVI) of R+10, which indicates a voting electorate that performs ten percentage points more Republican than the national average [3]. 

This voter guide provides a neutral, comprehensive, and detailed overview of the three candidates appearing on the general election ballot: incumbent Representative Kat Cammack (Republican), challenger Seth Harp (Democratic), and challenger Mike Klein (No Party Affiliation) [4, 5]. To ensure a strictly nonpartisan evaluation, the profiles below are structured identically, offering a side-by-side comparison of each candidate's professional background, stated policy positions, documented public record, campaign finance filings, and official endorsements.

## Side-by-Side Comparison of Stated Positions

To facilitate a direct, nonpartisan evaluation of the candidates, the following table compares their verified policy positions across major issue categories based on official platforms, legislative actions, and public statements [8, 9, 12, 24, 25, 36, 37, 38]. 

| Issue Category | Kat Cammack (Republican) | Seth Harp (Democratic) | Mike Klein (No Party Affiliation) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Economy, Taxes & Labor** | Advocates for minimizing government spending and keeping taxes low. Sponsored legislation (REINS Act) to limit the economic impact of executive branch regulations [9, 12]. | Proposes raising the corporate tax rate to 26% and taxing executive stock awards. Advocates capping CEO pay at 150x the median worker salary [24]. | Proposes a basic income floor for families facing an AI-driven economy. Advocates for antitrust enforcement to break monopolies and support fair wages [38]. |
| **Healthcare** | Emphasizes free-market principles; maintains a legislative record opposing the expansion of government-run healthcare and focusing on deregulation [10, 12]. | Guarantees affordable healthcare for all. Proposes doubling the behavioral health workforce over a decade via the D.O. Initiative [24, 25]. | Focuses on breaking prescription drug monopolies. Advocates for veteran-informed care in private civilian hospitals and investments in addiction treatment [25, 38]. |
| **Social Security & Safety Nets** | Platforms heavily on budget conservatism and reducing the national deficit, opposing broad safety net expansions [9, 10]. | Proposes stabilizing Social Security by raising the payroll tax cap to $250,000 [24, 25]. | Pledges to protect Social Security and lower the overarching cost of living for rural and working-class families [35]. |
| **Foreign Policy & Defense** | Vocal supporter of the U.S.-Israel alliance. Voted against major foreign aid packages (e.g., Ukraine). Supports high defense spending and troop readiness [8, 9, 14]. | Emphasizes domestic stability and middle-class rebuilding; does not feature foreign policy prominently in his core platform [11, 24]. | Campaigns on a "Strength Through Peace" pillar, prioritizing global leadership through diplomacy rather than military intervention [37]. |
| **Second Amendment** | Maintains strong support for the Second Amendment; backed legislative efforts to repeal federal regulations on firearm stabilizing braces [10, 12]. | Issued an "F" grade by the NRA-Political Victory Fund regarding his stances on gun control and firearm regulations [27]. | No verified information found regarding specific firearm policy platforms or Second Amendment stances. |
| **Governance & Ethics** | Voted affirmatively to ban Members of Congress from trading individual stocks [13, 14]. | Advocates for closing corporate tax loopholes and ensuring the government works for working people [20, 24]. | Identifies systemic corruption as the primary threat to democracy; demands the removal of corporate PAC money from politics [5, 35, 36]. |

**Establishing Research Scope**

I am initiating a comprehensive investigation into the 2026 general election for Florida's 3rd Congressional District. **Initial Candidate Assessment**

I am currently synthesizing the profiles of the three primary candidates for the 2026 race in Florida’s 3rd Congressional District. The incumbent, Kat Cammack, is positioning herself as a veteran legislator with a focus on national security, tech policy, and fiscal conservatism, supported by a substantial fundraising advantage. Her challengers include Seth Harp, a civics teacher and former broadcaster running on an affordability platform, and Mike Klein, an independent candidate and Army veteran whose campaign centers on removing corporate influence from the political system. I have observed that while the incumbent holds a massive financial lead, both challengers are leveraging specific professional backgrounds—education and military service—to appeal to the district's diverse electorate.

candidateProfileExample.name: Kat Cammack
candidateProfileExample.summary: Kat Cammack is the Republican incumbent representing Florida's 3rd Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives. First elected to Congress in 2020, she is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. Her platform focuses on border security, regulatory reduction, fiscal conservatism, and support for agricultural and small business interests.

background.label: Occupation
background.text: According to her official congressional biography and campaign materials, Cammack has worked as a small business owner, political strategist, and deputy chief of staff for former U.S. Representative Ted Yoho.

background.label: Education
background.text: According to her official biography and Ballotpedia, Cammack earned a Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2011 and a Master of Science in National Defense and Strategic Studies from the United States Naval War College in 2018.

background.label: Prior Public Offices
background.text: According to Ballotpedia and the Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Cammack has served as the U.S. Representative for Florida's 3rd Congressional District since taking office in January 2021.

positions.label: Economy and Government Spending
positions.text: According to her campaign and congressional websites, Cammack advocates for lower taxes, reduced federal spending, and regulatory reform, including sponsoring the REINS Act to require congressional approval for major executive agency rules.

positions.label: Border Security and Immigration
positions.text: According to her campaign website, Cammack supports strict enforcement of immigration laws and prioritizing physical and technological security along the U.S. southern border.

positions.label: Second Amendment
positions.text: According to her campaign website, Cammack supports defending Second Amendment gun ownership rights and opposes federal legislation that restricts firearm access for law-abiding citizens.

positions.label: Agriculture and Rural Affairs
positions.text: According to her official congressional statements, Cammack prioritizes protections and disaster assistance for Florida farmers and ranchers through federal Farm Bill legislation and agricultural relief programs.

funding.label: Federal Campaign Finance Totals
funding.text: According to Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings for the 2025–2026 election cycle through July 29, 2026, Cammack's principal campaign committee, Kat for Congress, reported $2,045,294 in total receipts, $1,723,874 in total disbursements, and $876,971 in cash on hand.

endorsements.label: Public Endorsements
endorsements.text: According to Ballotpedia and organization press releases, Cammack has been endorsed by former President Donald Trump and the political action committee Maggie's List.
